claims.head: Hinds and Luneau get the Thompson assignment
claims.call: The Ducks’ P2 (Hinds and Luneau) spends at least 37% of its 5-on-5 time against the Sabres’ second line.
claims.body: At home, the Ducks keep sending Hinds and Luneau out against opponents’ second lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Joel Quenneville has been picking a defense pair for opponents’ second lines. Tonight the Sabres’ second line is Benson, Thompson and Helenius.

notes.text: The forward lines keep changing. Even their four most-used trios over the last 10 games cover only 32% of their forwards’ 5-on-5 time, the 8th-lowest in the league (a typical team: 43%). The lines listed lean on their latest games, but expect new combinations tonight.
Konsta Helenius is out, reported after he played in their last game.
Jason Zucker was added to the roster on Oct 22 and has played beside Tage Thompson and Josh Norris.
Zach Metsa has started killing penalties: on the ice for 46% of the team’s shorthanded time in 11 games, up from 7% last season.
Josh Norris has started killing penalties: on the ice for 32% of the team’s shorthanded time in 12 games, up from 1% last season.

ANA.head: A slightly uphill night for the Ducks
ANA.body: Buffalo has been out-chancing opponents lately, but Anaheim has home-ice advantage. The Ducks’ best way to tip it is a power play that gets going.

BUF.head: Leaning the Sabres’ way
BUF.body: Buffalo has been out-chancing opponents lately, but Anaheim has home-ice advantage. The Ducks can still swing it if their power play gets going.

items.text: Olen Zellweger faces Anaheim for the first time since leaving.
The Sabres are newly without Konsta Helenius, and have had to make do without Alex Lyon all season. Colten Ellis is expected to start.
The Ducks are newly without Nikita Klepov and Pavel Mintyukov, and have had to make do without Troy Terry all season.
Jackson LaCombe has a point in four straight games.
